Yes. The papers say LLMs can suggest experiments or candidates directly without task-specific training, using zero-shot or few-shot prompting and text-based descriptions [1, 10]. In materials science, one framework explicitly calls itself training-free and proposes experiments in an iterative few-shot active-learning setting, while another uses LLMs as analogical chemists to generate novel materials from prompts and labeled examples [1, 2].

More broadly, the review says LLMs are already being used across materials discovery, including mining literature and coordinating experimental systems [4]. Some papers focus on broader exploration or optimization loops rather than direct experiment suggestion alone [5, 6, 9].
